- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent prices are falling.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >75% from prior day) are common; cap forecast at +10–15% above prior peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts when true outcome deviates >15% from 14d moving average; adjust forecast toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or weak.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00 or 0.33 → -0.33), reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for momentum decay.
- For 30d horizon, avoid extrapolating from 18d history without sentiment confirmation; if sentiment is volatile, use 7d average as anchor for correction.
